newsitem.title: USA: IMF sees further recovery of growth in Austria.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees further recovery of growth in Austria.

text.p: Austria's economy is likely to stage a continued recovery in 1997 and beyond, but initially it will lag the European Union's overall projected growth rate, the International Monetary Fund said Friday.

The IMF, which issued the outlook after completing regular bilateral discussions with Austria, projected the country's 1997 real gross domestic product would rise by 1.7 percent, after increasing by 1 percent in 1996.

"The expansion will initially be narrowly based on exports and investment, with consumption remaining subdued due to continued fiscal consolidation and stagnating disposable income," the IMF said in a statement.
Wage moderation and persisent output gaps will keep inflation low, the IMF said. But unemployment is expected to decline only after 1997, it added.
IMF directors commended Austrian officials for "maintaining financial stability and implementing a bold fiscal adjustment effort."
They agreed that ongoing fiscal consolidation and structural reforms were needed to boost confidence, bolster efficiency and create conditions for sustainable growth and the creation of new jobs.

The IMF directors stressed the importance of sticking to the well-publicized federal deficit target levels for 1997. They said further fiscal consolidation would be needed beyond 1997 to reduce the debt ratio.

The IMF emphasized the need for flexible labor and product markets to deal with future shocks and to enhance Austria's growth prospects. The directors urged authorities to step up efforts to deregulate the economy and privatize state-owned companies.
Directors supported the long-standing exchange rate peg, which had promoted financial stability and economic integration with Austria's neighbors.
Austrian authorities were also encouraged to reverse the decline in offical development assistance.
